test_findings.test: second concurrent call with used >= limit throws QuotaExceededError
test_findings.detail: Replaces the round-1 circular/vacuous AC8 test and addresses the round-1 'important' concurrency gap. It fires two overlapping checkAndIncrementQuota calls; the first (mock count LIMIT-1) resolves below limit and the second (mock count LIMIT) throws QuotaExceededError, guarding the at/above-limit boundary. Minor note (non-blocking): it uses two independent DbClient mocks rather than one shared atomic counter, so it validates the boundary throw logic rather than true upsert atomicity under contention — which is inherently unreproducible with a mocked DB, consistent with the round-1 caveat.

test_findings.detail: Unchanged from round 1 and outside the delta. The increment guarantee is supplied by the mock's returned row; strengthening by asserting the upsert SQL contains an increment expression remains a non-blocking suggestion.

test_findings.test: renders null (nothing) when the API returns 401 / non-ok / network error
test_findings.detail: The fetch assertion pins the exact call signature fetch('/api/me/download-quota', { method: 'GET' }). The contract only requires 'fetches GET /api/me/download-quota on mount', so a bare fetch(url) (which defaults to GET) would fail this assertion. This slightly over-constrains the implementation but is a reasonable convention and non-blocking; the coder controls the impl per contract.
